_comment: OHAO golden-image regression corpus. Run from repo root.
_what_this_gate_actually_is: Read this before trusting a green run, and before loosening anything.
These scenes are Monte Carlo path traces. The renderer is deterministic for
a fixed sampler and a fixed build -- two runs are byte-identical -- so this
corpus is, in practice, a HASH of an unchanged sampler with enough slack for
the GPU floating-point floor. It is not a tolerance gate in the sense of
'the image is still about right', and it cannot be made into one by raising
the sample count. Measured on cornell_box against a 1024 spp reference:
16 spp is max_abs 88 / rmse 10.8, 64 spp is 47 / 6.9, 256 spp is 34 / 4.1.
Noise falls as 1/sqrt(N), so a max_abs 4 tolerance is out of reach at any
sample count anyone will wait for.
WHAT IT CATCHES: a changed shader, a changed material, a broken pass, a
missing asset -- anything that moves pixels while the sample sequence stays
put. That is the common case and the gate is genuinely good at it.
WHAT IT CANNOT DISTINGUISH: a real regression from any change that perturbs
the sample SEQUENCE (a new sampler dimension, a reordered bounce, a changed
seed). Both reshuffle every pixel by the noise magnitude. When you change
sampling, this corpus will go red and it cannot tell you whether you also
broke something. Verify that case by eye or with a converged render.
max_abs_diff 4 is sized for the cross-session GPU floor, not for noise. The
same SPIR-V on the same machine has been measured drifting 3 channels of
6.2M by 1 LSB between sessions; 4 covers that with margin.
_growing: Denoiser OFF on every scene: we pin raw deterministic beauty. A denoiser is a large, version-dependent, non-linear prior, and pinning its output pins the denoiser rather than the renderer.
Grow this list as features land -- every fixed bug should add a scene so it cannot silently regress. A scene costs one entry here and a few seconds a run.

A scene must load only TRACKED assets, or it is not a gate on a fresh clone. Not a style rule: the scene this replaced pointed at a file nobody had, and its empty render was reported as a pixel regression for two months.
_regenerating: It overwrites without comparing, so it cannot tell an intentional refresh
from laundering a regression. Look at what drifted FIRST. The goldens these
replaced were 78 renderer commits stale and nobody knew, because the harness
could not run at all on a multi-config generator.

scenes.name: cornell_box
scenes._note: Builds its scene in code and loads no asset, so it runs on a bare clone.

scenes.name: damaged_helmet
scenes._note: Replaces metal_rough_spheres, whose MetalRoughSpheres.glb was never in the repository. model_viewer used to exit 0 after a failed load and render an empty frame, so that scene reported a large pixel difference for two months instead of a missing file. DamagedHelmet.glb IS tracked (3.7 MB) and covers the same ground: a metal/rough glTF under an HDRI.
scenes._recaptured: 2026-10-10, sub-project 2a Task 8 (RT reads RenderScene). The old golden was NOT lit by the HDRI: the legacy RT build loaded the env map before any path tracer existed, so it took bindless index 0 -- the first wall's 1x1 solid-color layer -- and every miss ray returned that constant color. The new path registers the HDRI in the one texture table. Verified at 1024 spp against master: with the old index emulated, master vs new is max_abs 9 / frac>4 0.0002 inside the helmet box and 8 / 0.0001 outside (640-wide); with the real HDRI the whole frame changes (mean RGB 130 -> 98). Albedo/emissive textures are now sRGB-decoded by the sampler instead of pow(2.2) on UNORM; the helmet's textures were already sampled at their native 2048^2.

scenes.name: cornell_box_deferred
scenes._note: Deferred hybrid (G-buffer + RT shadows/GI where supported). Captured on master before sub-project 2a so the ECS/RenderScene migration is checked against the old renderer's own output. Exact since sub-project 4 step 1 (2026-10-23): deferred rendering is bit-identical run to run, ten separate-process renders gave one pixel hash, and this golden has measured max_abs 0 in every session since 2026-10-09. Any difference is a change to look at, not noise.

scenes.name: damaged_helmet_deferred
scenes._note: Deferred hybrid on the helmet with TAA, SSAO and bloom; same purpose as cornell_box_deferred. Exact since sub-project 4 step 1 (2026-10-23). It used to move run to run (max_abs 1-5, ~2.6% of pixels) because bloom's mip chain read each mip before the previous render pass's writes were visible, and TAA's first frame read an unset previous view-projection; both are fixed, ten separate-process renders gave one pixel hash, and the golden was regenerated then (the old one differed by max_abs 1 on 2.9% of pixels, scattered: one sample of the race).

scenes.name: cornell_box_rt_realtime
scenes._note: Realtime path tracer (ReSTIR GI reservoirs, temporal history, 19 frames). Added 2026-10-10 after it lost the device and wrote an all-black frame on master and on this branch: bindings 29-35 (reservoirs, spec hit-distance) were never written into the descriptor set. A black frame fails here twice -- the uniform-frame check and max_abs 225. Not bit-exact run-to-run: pt_raygen_realtime.rgen reads accumBuffer/normalAOV at neighbour pixels in the same dispatch that writes them, a race. Fresh-vs-fresh measured max_abs 3-5, diff_frac ~0.015 at compare res, hence 10 / 0.05.

scenes.name: cli_cornell_box
scenes._note: Scene goldens (reflection spec, step 9): the checked-in scene file rendered by the ohao CLI must match the golden the example renders from code. Same PNG, same tolerance as cornell_box; a separate golden would let the two drift apart.

scenes.name: cli_cornell_box_deferred
scenes._note: As cli_cornell_box, against cornell_box_deferred's golden. 10 frames and no post effects: what the example does. Exact, as cornell_box_deferred: the example and the CLI give the same pixels.

scenes.name: cli_damaged_helmet_deferred
scenes._note: As cli_cornell_box, against damaged_helmet_deferred's golden. model_viewer renders 30 deferred frames with TAA, SSAO and bloom on at exposure 1 (the renderer's own default is 0.6); the scene file holds no render settings, so the command line states them. Exact, as damaged_helmet_deferred: the example and the CLI give the same pixels.
